title: Proof collaboration-server persisted authority and assembled configuration artifacts
description: The root entrypoint accepts only a persisted signed remote-authority envelope or an assembled EnvironmentConfigV2 projection. Raw authority facts below are decoded-payload/result definitions and are never persisted unsigned.

effectiveConstraints.description: Exact effective CAP numeric constraint closure. This intentionally reuses the accepted AuthorizationDecisionV2 shape byte-for-byte.

operatingBindingEvaluation.description: Exact operating Agent binding state at the evaluated authority head. A present revocation record always makes the binding inactive; an active binding cannot carry a revocation record. Inactivity can also result from validity-window evaluation, so active:false does not by itself require a revocation record.

delegationEvaluation.description: Exact DelegationV2 resolution at the same evaluated authority head as the decision. A hidden or absent delegation is deliberately indistinguishable.

requestedResources.description: Exact accepted AuthorizationDecisionV2 requested-resources projection. Every array is duplicate-free and sorted by UTF-8 bytes before evaluation or digesting.

agentAuthorization.description: Closed Agent-only authorization closure, shaped after accepted AuthorizationDecisionV2. Authentication binds the signed selector; this object records resolution and CAP evaluation at the decision head.

authorizationReasonCode.description: Closed signed decision union vocabulary: the accepted direct-Agent denial set, the Human-only disclosure-safe generic denial, and the allow marker. proof.authorization.denied is not an Agent-direct source reason; an Agent policy_denied or chain_unsupported source reason may still project to that caller-safe public code.

agentDirectAuthorizationReasonCode.description: Closed accepted proof.local/authority/direct/v1 Agent vocabulary. It deliberately excludes the Human-only proof.authorization.denied source reason.

publicAuthorizationCode.description: Closed caller-safe denial projection. Exact source-to-public membership remains selected by the bound operation/profile registry row.

applicationProblemCode.description: Closed global caller-safe application-failure vocabulary. The exact committed registry row selects a subset.

applicationProblemDigestCode.description: Closed failure-code vocabulary for the application consequence digest preimage. Precondition conflict is already part of applicationProblemCode; idempotency conflict adds its one reserved code.

applicationProblemDigestPreimageV1.title: ApplicationProblemDigestPreimageV1
applicationProblemDigestPreimageV1.description: The complete stable caller-safe failure projection hashed by RemoteApplicationConsequenceV1. HTTP type, title, status, retryability, retry delay, instance, operation_id, correlation_id, findings, current_digest, headers, detail, and private diagnostics are deliberately outside this authority preimage.

workspaceRoleAssignmentV1.title: WorkspaceRoleAssignmentV1
workspaceRoleAssignmentV1.description: Decoded append-only authority payload. This v1 assignment has no expiry; only an append-only revocation ends it.

workspaceRoleRevocationV1.title: WorkspaceRoleRevocationV1
workspaceRoleRevocationV1.description: Append-only revocation of one exact active role assignment; it never edits the assignment.

reason.description: Authoritative normalized reason copied from the workspace-role.revoke/v1 request into the immutable signed revocation payload.

changeSetApprovalV1.title: ChangeSetApprovalV1
changeSetApprovalV1.description: Inequality and digest-coherence rules are normative semantic validation rules represented by rejected vectors.

normalizedEnvironmentConfiguration.description: The environment_config_digest and normalized_configuration_digest are both the RFC 8785 digest of this object under proof:environment-config:v2.

environmentConfigActivationV1.title: EnvironmentConfigActivationV1
environmentConfigActivationV1.description: activated_by_principal_id must differ from the proposal's proposed_by_principal_id.

environmentConfigV2.title: EnvironmentConfigV2
environmentConfigV2.description: Immutable active configuration assembled from and cross-checked against the exact proposal and activation authority records.
x-proof-semantic-equalities: environment_creation fields copied into activation equal environment_creation

environmentCreationV1.title: EnvironmentCreationV1
environmentCreationV1.description: Decoded immutable authority payload establishing one Environment's creation chronology.

remotePrincipalStatusV2.title: RemotePrincipalStatusV2
remotePrincipalStatusV2.description: The first online server profile permits only terminal disablement. Re-enablement requires separately qualified offline recovery.

reason.description: Authoritative normalized disablement reason copied from principal-status.set/v2 into this immutable signed status payload.

remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.title: RemoteAuthorizationDecisionV1
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.description: One server-produced current-head authorization decision. Cross-field actor, policy, presentation-consumption, role, and projection rules require semantic validation.
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.x-proof-public-input-projection-rule: public_input_projection_digest equals the same proof:public-operation-input-projection:v1 digest carried by the exact public AuthenticatedActorContextEvidenceV2. Human operation inputs use the operation-specific disclosure-safe projection declared by their input contract; Agent operations use the exact signed normalized_input. For oidc-binding.issue/v1 the projection contains the retry-stabilized blinded subject_commitment and pinned issuer-configuration digest but neither raw issuer/subject nor their private exact-input digest. The private idempotency/input digest is retained only inside protected storage.
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.x-proof-actor-context-digest-rule: actor_context_digest equals the proof:authenticated-actor-context-evidence:v2 digest of the exact public-safe AuthenticatedActorContextEvidenceV2 produced for this request; the private runtime context, raw issuer/subject, session handle, token, or request-carried actor selector is never the preimage.
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.x-proof-operation-registry-rule: operation_registry_sha256 is lowercase SHA-256 over RFC 8785 of the complete exact HttpOperationRegistryV1 value used for this decision, including the selected operation row's input/result schemas, idempotency, concurrency, consequence/effect rule, and application_problem_codes. A portable verifier accepts the decision only when this exact hash resolves through the independently pinned VerificationTrustPolicyV2 offline registry profile. The resolved full registry's embedded authorization_registry_commitment.authorization_registry_sha256 must equal this decision's signed authorization_registry_sha256 byte-for-byte; membership in two independent allowlists never permits cross-version pairing. authorization_registry_sha256 separately commits the authorization-only projection and cannot substitute for the full selector.
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.x-proof-requested-resources-digest-rule: Resolve authorization_rule in the exact authorization catalog committed by authorization_registry_sha256, which is lowercase SHA-256 over RFC 8785 of exactly {agent_authorization_projection,authorization_resource_projection,authorization_rule_definitions,human_authorization_projection}. The Human projection freezes each operation's requested action, rule and roles; the Agent projection freezes each operation's accepted direct-policy mapping. For an Agent row, agent_authorization.requested_resources is the exact accepted AuthorizationDecisionV2 projection and the catalog declares its eight field names as the structured bindings. For each exact structured resource binding, value_digest is BLAKE3-256 derive-key proof:authorization-resource-binding:v1 over RFC 8785 of {api_version:proof.dev/authorization-resource-binding/v1,name,value:<exact normalized public-safe typed value>}. requested_resources_digest is BLAKE3-256 derive-key proof:requested-authorization-resources:v1 over RFC 8785 of {api_version:proof.dev/requested-authorization-resources/v1,authorization_registry_sha256,authorization_rule,operation,requested_action,bindings:[{name,value_digest}...]}. Bindings are unique and sorted by UTF-8 name; composite selectors are separate bindings. OIDC issuance may bind the public subject_commitment and issuer-configuration digest but never raw issuer, subject, blind, token, code, session, or a private exact-input digest.
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.x-proof-policy-bundle-digest-rule: policy_bundle_digest is BLAKE3-256 derive-key proof:remote-authorization-policy-selection:v1 over RFC 8785 of {api_version:proof.dev/remote-authorization-policy-selection/v1,authorization_registry_sha256,authorization_rule,environment_config_digest,environment_policy_bundle_digest}. environment_policy_bundle_digest is recovered from the exact EnvironmentConfigV2 named by environment_config_digest and is null exactly when environment_config_digest is null. This makes the committed catalog rule the explicit built-in policy for non-Environment rows and additionally binds the selected Environment policy for Environment rows; neither the catalog hash alone nor an ambient current policy may substitute.
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.x-proof-effective-constraints-rule: For a resolved DelegationV2, agent_authorization.effective_constraints is the component-wise minimum of that immutable delegation's three numeric constraints and any stricter exact operation/request ceilings. For not_found_or_hidden, it is the deterministic operation/request ceiling computed without a delegation and conveys no authority; the decision is necessarily deny with delegation_unavailable. allow_subdelegation remains a Delegation fact and is deliberately absent from this accepted three-field decision shape.
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.x-proof-authority-closure-rule: All referenced authority records resolve at evaluated_authority_head. The requesting binding is active and matches the requesting Principal and commitment. For Agent decisions, agent_authorization command, presentation, operating identity and historical binding fields equal the actor evidence; current binding/delegation records and revocations resolve at the same head. Resolved DelegationV2 bytes reproduce the delegation record digest and the exact policy/request/constraint evaluation inputs. For allow, those bytes bind the same requesting/operating Principals and Workspace, authorize requested_action/resources, and satisfy current binding/principal/time/scope/budget state at evaluated_at. For deny, the verifier evaluates those same immutable bytes under x-proof-agent-denial-precedence-rule, including the identity-mismatch branch. role_assignment_digests are the unique UTF-8-sorted active assignment-record digests actually used; an allow contains every role assignment required by its exact rule, while a missing-role denial may carry none. environment_config_digest is null exactly when the rule resolves no Environment; otherwise it is the selected active EnvironmentConfigV2 digest. The outer policy_bundle_digest follows the exact policy-selection digest rule, never an unspecified ambient policy.
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.x-proof-agent-denial-precedence-rule: For the accepted direct Agent profile, current requesting- or operating-Principal disablement is evaluated before binding state, binding state before Delegation availability, and availability before resolving the exact referenced DelegationV2. Once resolved, an issuer_principal_id/requesting_principal_id or recipient_principal_id/operating_principal_id mismatch selects scope_exceeded before Delegation revocation; a matching Delegation with a resolved revocation selects delegation_revoked; only an unrevoked matching Delegation reaches validity-window, action/resource scope, budget, and policy checks. Therefore either principal_state enabled flag being false selects principal_disabled even if later closure fields are also adverse; with both Principals enabled, binding.active false selects binding_inactive. JSON Schema cannot compare identities held in the referenced Delegation bytes, so semantic validation distinguishes the pre-revocation identity-mismatch scope_exceeded branch from later action/resource scope_exceeded branches, which require a null revocation. active true requires null binding revocation, while inactive can result from time/rotation with a null revocation record.
remoteAuthorizationDecisionV1.x-proof-decision-rule: The decision extends evaluated_authority_head exactly: authority_sequence is head.sequence + 1 and previous_authority_record_digest equals head.record_digest. Allow requires reason_code proof.authorization.allowed and public_code null. Deny requires a non-null caller-safe public_code equal to the operation/profile disclosure projection of reason_code. Every identity, operation, projection, command/presentation, and head field equals the referenced actor evidence; no caller-supplied selector may substitute for that evidence.

remoteApplicationConsequenceV1.title: RemoteApplicationConsequenceV1
remoteApplicationConsequenceV1.description: Signed consequence of one proven and authorized committed attempt. result_digest is always non-null and preserves the accepted application digest contract: BLAKE3-256 derive-key proof:operation-effect:v1 over the RFC 8785 exact result_schema data on success/replay, or over the exact applicationProblemDigestPreimageV1 {api_version, code, operation} on a committed non-success. HTTP Problem status, title, detail, instance, and extensions never enter this digest preimage.
remoteApplicationConsequenceV1.x-proof-decision-closure-rule: Resolve decision_digest as BLAKE3-256 derive-key proof:remote-authority-record:v1 over the exact canonical RemoteAuthorizationDecisionV1. That decision is allow, decision_id matches, and workspace_id, operation, operation_registry_sha256, public_input_projection_digest, application_key_kind, and the exact request-or-derived application_key identify this attempt. operation_registry_sha256 equals the decision's signed full-registry selector and is independently accepted by the verifier trust policy. Resolve exactly one committed operation row by the tuple (operation.name, operation.version, containing route.authentication), where route.authentication equals decision.authentication_profile; name and version alone are not a row selector because Human and Agent routes can carry distinct rows for the same operation. A Human selection must equal the exact human_authorization_projection entry and the row authorization_rule, requested_action, and roles projection bound by the decision; an Agent selection requires proof.local/authority/direct/v1 and must equal the exact agent_authorization_projection entry and row requested_action/consequence projection. Resolve the effect, idempotency, result, and application-failure rules only from that route-qualified row. For an authority-record success, the governed effect payload is appended immediately after the decision and application_effect_authority_head names it; this consequence appends immediately after that effect. For every other success or non-success, application_effect_authority_head is null and this consequence appends immediately after the decision. Every evaluated head, predecessor, sequence, and recorded time follows the selected branch exactly. A consequence cannot bind an unrelated decision, registry, operation, route authentication profile, authorization projection, input, key, Workspace, effect, or stale head.
remoteApplicationConsequenceV1.x-proof-authority-effect-branch-rule: When outcome is success and the selected registry effect_digest_rule has digest_context proof:remote-authority-record:v1, application_effect_authority_head is non-null, its record_digest equals application_effect_digest, and the exact canonical governed effect payload has previous_authority_record_digest equal to decision_digest and authority_sequence equal to decision.authority_sequence + 1. When that payload Schema defines evaluated_authority_head (the collaboration-server successor authority payloads), it also equals {record_digest:decision_digest,sequence:decision.authority_sequence}; the accepted legacy PrincipalBindingV1, PrincipalBindingRevocationV1, DelegationV2 and DelegationRevocationV1 bytes do not define that member and must not be extended with it. The committed registry effect_timestamp_field selects the exact payload timestamp (issued_at, revoked_at, assigned_at, approved_at, proposed_at, activated_at or recorded_at); that selected timestamp is not earlier than decision.evaluated_at, and consequence.recorded_at is not earlier than the selected timestamp. This consequence's evaluated_authority_head and previous_authority_record_digest equal application_effect_digest, authority_sequence equals decision.authority_sequence + 2, and application_effect_authority_head.sequence equals the effect payload authority_sequence. For all other registry effect rules and every non-success outcome, application_effect_authority_head is null; evaluated_authority_head and previous_authority_record_digest equal decision_digest, authority_sequence equals decision.authority_sequence + 1, and recorded_at is not earlier than decision.evaluated_at. This ordering prevents a governed authority fact and its signed consequence from occupying the same causal position or predating its authorizing decision.
remoteApplicationConsequenceV1.x-proof-idempotency-row-rule: Use only the unique route-qualified operation row selected by (operation.name, operation.version, decision.authentication_profile) from the complete exact registry committed by operation_registry_sha256, and require application_key_kind to equal that row's application_idempotency. required-uuidv7 uses the exact UUIDv7 input key bound by public_input_projection_digest; none uses null; derived-changeset and derived-proposal-policy-validator use a BLAKE3 digest. A derived-changeset key is proof:operation-effect:v1 over RFC 8785 {api_version:proof.dev/application-idempotency-key/v1,changeset_id,operation:changeset.submit/v2,workspace_id}. A derived-proposal-policy-validator key uses the same context over RFC 8785 {api_version:proof.dev/application-idempotency-key/v1,changeset_id,operation:changeset.validate/v2,policy_digest,proposal_digest,validator,workspace_id}; every component is in the decision-bound resolved closure. Only success reserves the successful key/result/effect tuple. Replay resolves the same operation/profile/key's stored successful tuple and requires result_digest == prior_result_digest == that stored success result digest. Idempotency conflict requires the same operation/profile/key's stored successful row and prior_result_digest equal to that row's result digest, while result_digest commits the exact idempotency failure preimage; the conflict does not replace the stored row. Other failures do not reserve a successful row.
remoteApplicationConsequenceV1.x-proof-result-digest-rule: For success and idempotent-replay, result_digest is BLAKE3-256 derive-key proof:operation-effect:v1 over RFC 8785 of the exact result_schema value selected by the unique route-qualified committed registry row; replay requires exact equality with the stored successful result and prior_result_digest. For idempotency-conflict, precondition-conflict and application-failure, the complete digest preimage is applicationProblemDigestPreimageV1: {api_version:proof.dev/application-problem-digest-preimage/v1,code:problem_code,operation}; no other Problem or transport field participates. For application-failure, problem_code must belong to that same route-qualified row's exact post-Allow application_problem_codes set. A code present only in the same operation's row under another authentication profile is forbidden. Authentication, authorization, infrastructure, and transport failures absent from the selected set are forbidden; a legacy code prefix does not override explicit source-contract reachability. No row-specific or caller-selected digest context is permitted.
remoteApplicationConsequenceV1.x-proof-effect-digest-rule: All non-success outcomes require application_effect_digest null. On success, resolve the exact registry row consequence: governed immutable-effect rows require application_effect_digest to equal that exact consequence artifact's documented domain-separated digest, while rows declared authority-evidence-only or read-only require null. The effect digest never names transport bytes or an outbox projection, and a generic consequence class cannot substitute for the row's exact effect rule.
remoteApplicationConsequenceV1.x-proof-delivery-management-rule: For delivery.replay/v1 or delivery.abandon/v1 success, application_effect_digest is the proof:delivery-management-fact:v1 digest of the immutable application fact; that fact is not an authority payload, and this signed consequence is its authority binding.

remoteAuthorityRecordV1.title: RemoteAuthorityRecordV1
remoteAuthorityRecordV1.description: Closed runtime authority payload union. Existing local artifact versions retain their accepted bytes; the remote decision supplies the remote actor evidence for reused administrative facts.

remoteAuthorityRecordEnvelopeV1.title: RemoteAuthorityRecordV1 DSSE envelope
remoteAuthorityRecordEnvelopeV1.description: The decoded payload must be canonical RFC 8785 JSON, validate as remoteAuthorityRecordV1, and be signed by the independently resolved causally active Workspace authority key over DSSE PAE bytes.

payload.description: Canonical standard Base64. Semantic validation also decodes before enforcing the exact 65,536-byte payload bound.
